title: Feeling pleasure between one more repetition

captions.physics: Repeating pleasure for an immediate reward
captions.emotions: Understanding an impression at your pace

meaning: A quiet pause supports leisure together when repetition and abundance leave too little time to notice what already delighted both.
text: Pleasure can repeat faster than it becomes an impression. The Devil in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes actions tied to immediate reward: continuing, repeating and holding onto something successful. The Empress in energy leans towards adding richness. The Hermit in emotions allows what you received to be understood at your own pace. A quiet response may need stopping even while more pleasure remains available and using it all today seems necessary. Availability alone need not decide what either person actually wants now.

For example, you take turns opening small jars of different fragrances. One scent brings a pleasant memory, but hands already reach for the next and expanding the selection appeals. **Shared pleasure needs time to become experience you have lived.** You can pause over one fragrance and tell each other what it recalls. Another jar remains a free possibility, beyond competing with a quiet joy already present or proving the evening rich and equally absorbing for both.

The difficulty is treating restraint as insufficient stimulation. You offer more, change the order and hear actual impressions less. Attention moves towards the next promise instead of experiencing what arrived. A pause preserves togetherness while permitting satisfaction, individual pace and free continuation. Leisure can stay warm with unused materials and without immediately explaining why simply sitting quietly beside each other now feels pleasant.
